sections.content:
28,805 people

were counted on the census as "environment professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Environment professionals investigate, address, and advise on resource management issues relating to land and marine environments. They develop and implement environmental policies and remedies that address the impacts of human activities and industrial processes on the environment.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "environment professionals", 14.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "environment professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "environment professionals" included:

  • other health professionals
  • business associate professionals (other)
  • early education and childcare services managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "environment professionals" there were more men than women (58.5% compared with 41.5%).

This means "environment professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 58.5% and women made up 41.5% of "environment professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "environment professionals" included:

  • managers and proprietors in other services (other)
  • specialist medical practitioners
  • data analysts

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "environment professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "environment professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "environment professionals", 9.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.7% compared with 13.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.9%) than self-employed (7.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Bristol, City of, this is in the region of the South West.
